text:
alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-probe change merged this morning we're seeing PP bubble growth on the 1F1B schedule for the 7B encoder-decoder model.
alex: baseline (before): steady tail ~6ms/microbatch, after probe: tail ~18ms/microbatch on p4d-8x.
maria: omg. which probe? the dynamic-kernel-selector that probes TF32 vs FP16 kernels?
alex: yes — the selector added a fallthrough path that does a quick kernel benchmark during first N steps. suspect it triggers extra syncs.
cheng: can you paste the perf summary from perf-bot? or the nsight snippet?
alex: perf-bot just posted this summary:
perf-bot: model=redwood-7B-v2 | schedule=1F1B | microbatch=4 | TP=2 PP=4 | baseline_latency=72ms -> current_latency=95ms | allreduce-tail=+9ms | kvcache-hit=54% (was 88%)
alex: the interesting bits: allreduce tail increased and kv cache hit rate dropped (evictions spiked). not sure if related to kernel probes causing different memory ordering.
sam: did the probe allocate temp buffers? our probe uses a small sanity run that creates a couple of intermediate tensors then frees them.
alex: yes it does an isolated kernel run, but it should be in-place and freed. logs show extra CUDA syncs around probe start/stop.
maria: can you share the small nsys capture? even 5s with perf markers would help.
alex: attached snippet from nsys (trimmed):
```
[ 0.002s ] kernel_probe_start
[ 0.003s ] launch kernel A (tf32)
[ 0.004s ] cudaDeviceSynchronize
[ 0.004s ] kernel_probe_end
[ 0.060s ] allreduce start
[ 0.069s ] allreduce end (tail)
```
alex: probe adds a sync at ~0.004s that pushes subsequent allreduce into a different overlap window — that's my hypothesis.
cheng: that sync could prevent comm/compute overlap. if we drop that sync, we might regain overlap and reduce the tail.
sam: quick experiment idea: make probe non-blocking (no cudaDeviceSynchronize) and instead rely on event queries. or run probe on a pinned CPU thread so it doesn't touch worker streams.
maria: also the KV cache eviction spike — maybe probe temp allocations cause allocator fragmentation, leading to smaller contiguous free chunks for KV pages.
alex: allocator logs show smaller max-free-chunk immediately after probe: 1.2GB -> 512MB.
perf-bot: suggested_action: rollback kernel-probe to previous commit; suggested_quicktest: run 1F1B microbatch=4/8 without probe.
cheng: rollback for canary is safest. but we should also add a non-blocking probe variant and stress-test for fragmentation.
sam: I'll put a canary rollback on the dedicated queue and run the benchmark job with microbatch sweep.
maria: also add a KV cache metric to the CI perf test: track hit-rate, largest-free-chunk, and eviction rate per step.
alex: quick command I'm running now (if you want to reproduce):
```
python -m perf.run --model redwood-7B-v2 --schedule 1F1B --microbatch 4 --tp 2 --pp 4 --probe true --trace nsys --duration 30
```
cheng: thanks. if rollback fixes it we can reintroduce a probe with: (1) no cuda syncs, (2) use stream + event to measure duration, (3) allocate probe buffers from a separate scratch allocator.
sam: I'll create the rollback PR and attach job ids. alex, can you paste the job ids here when done?
alex: job: 0x8a3f (canary with probe) and 0x8b22 (rollback). canary shows 95ms, rollback shows 73ms. attaching short logs.
maria: great — seems rollback recovers overlap. next: schedule an RFC for a safe probe design (non-blocking, allocator-isolated). include experiments on microbatch jitter and KV cache pressure.
cheng: add a perf test that toggles probe at step 0 and step 1000 to detect long-term fragmentation.
alex: agreed. action items:
- sam: roll back in canary + run sweep (inflight) (sam)
- alex: capture allocator traces & upload nsys (alex)
- maria: add KV cache metrics to CI perf harness (maria)
- cheng: draft RFC for non-blocking probe + scratch allocator (cheng)

alex: thanks everyone. tagging @perf-bot to keep an eye on regression alerts :eyes:
perf-bot: noted. will open incident if latency > +15% for 3 consecutive runs.
